citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility is not performing adequate daily observations in the bat enclosure. In the enclosure housing seven adult
Egyptian fruit bats, the inspector identified a small dead bat attached to back wall of the enclosure. The dead bat
appeared to be desiccated and had been scavenged by insects. The facility representative stated that they observe the
seven adult bats every day and that the group is capable of breeding; however, the facility did not notice that a new bat
had been born or that it had died.
Effective daily observations allow the facility to assess the health of the animals. Failure to observe medical problems,
including animal deaths, can result in prolonged illness and pain of individual animals and undetected colony/herd health
concerns. The facility must conduct daily observations of all animals to asses their health and well-being and then ensure
a mechanism of direct and frequent communication so that timely and accurate information on problems of health,
behavior, and well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian.

The facility is not adequately cleaning the enclosure for seven Egyptian fruit bats. The wire walls of the bat enclosure and
the wooden surfaces inside the enclosure are coated in a mottled brown material, especially below areas where the bats
hang from the ceiling. The inspector also saw multiple roaches below one of the dirty wooden structures. The facility
representative stated that they routinely change out the bedding at the bottom of the enclosure but it had been at least a
month since the walls and surfaces had been cleaned.
Inadequate cleaning can result in an accumulation of excreta and other waste in the enclosure, which can increase the
likelihood of disease hazards and attract pests. Excreta shall be removed from primary enclosures as often as necessary
to prevent contamination of the animals contained therein and to minimize disease hazards and to reduce odors.
To be corrected by June 26, 2026.

The facility does not have adequate pest control for roaches. The inspector saw multiple live roaches inside the enclosure
housing seven Egyptian fruit bats.
Pests such as roaches can spread disease and contaminate food, surfaces, and animal housing areas. A safe and
effective program for the control of insects, ectoparasites, and avian and mammalian pests shall be established and
maintained.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
